test_case.test_name: Parameterized Windows NIC driver installation, binding and rollback validation
test_case.purpose: Install the approved signed NIC driver on the target Windows build and verify correct device binding/version, no Device Manager warning and restored network function.
required_package: Exact Windows edition/build/architecture and patch state
NIC vendor/device/subsystem/PCI identity plus firmware compatibility
Secure Boot/signing and platform prerequisite policy
Affected-interface outage, reboot approval, independent console/OOB and uninstall/rollback image
test_case.test_command: Capture current Device Manager status, hardware IDs, driver provider/version/date and network configuration. Validate package signature/hash and compatibility, then run only the vendor-supported Windows installer with complete logs. If explicitly approved, reboot once; verify Device Manager has no yellow warning, expected binding/version and functional link/IP/traffic; preserve evidence and keep the rollback package available.
test_case.expected_result: Approved driver installs without installer/event error, binds to the exact NIC, Device Manager shows normal status with no warning, expected version is active and network function returns after any approved reboot.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires signed compatible package, exact Windows/NIC identity, successful install/binding/version, clean Device Manager/event evidence and functional recovery. Linux module evidence cannot pass this case.
safety_gate: Do not install before package signature/hash and hardware/OS compatibility are approved.
Require independent console/OOB before disrupting the active NIC.
No reboot unless explicitly included in the signed run contract.
Abort on wrong hardware ID, signature failure, loss of rollback path or unexpected interface outage; no automatic retry.
expected_evidence: Device Manager before/after screenshots or exported status
Link/IP/traffic recovery, reboot record and rollback readiness
test_case.recovery: On warning state, bad binding or lost networking, stop further install attempts, use independent console, preserve installer/SetupAPI/event evidence, apply only the approved vendor uninstall/rollback or known-good image, and require network/Windows owner verification before retry.
